In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

arc magmatism in south-central Chile has been driven by a combination of crustal thick-ening and subduction erosion, both of which have been episodic in the past ~25 m. y. and are linked to episodic eastward migration of arc segments.
the Andean Southern Central Volcanic Zone is not a simple linear arc, but a highly complex, episodically migrating system with a history of crustal thickning, magmatism, and subduction erosion.
the arc system in this region has been migrating to the east at a rate of 10–15 km/m.y. over the last 20 m.y., with episodic changes in the chemistry of the magma production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
“the Andes is a dynamic place.”
the Andes is a very dynamic system, and that the geologic record of the Southern Volicanic Zone shows that it has been so for at least 25 million years.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Andean Southern Central Volcanic Zone is an active, dynamic, evolving arc system.
subduction erosion can have a major impact on the evolution of magmatic arcs.
